title: Batch rename objects by rule
purpose: Rename many objects at once by rule: strip .001 suffixes, find and replace with optional regular expressions, apply a case style, add a prefix and suffix, and number only the names that would collide. Use it to prepare scenes for export and naming conventions.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: Text put in front of every name (not repeated when already present).

parameters.name: suffix
parameters.description: Text put after every name, before any number.

parameters.name: find
parameters.description: Text or regular expression to replace; empty skips this step.

parameters.name: replace
parameters.description: Replacement for find; with use_regex it may use groups such as \1.

parameters.name: use_regex
parameters.description: Treat find as a Python regular expression.

parameters.name: case
parameters.description: Case style applied to the words of the name.

parameters.name: numbering
parameters.description: Number every name, only names that would collide, or none.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: First number of a numbered group.

parameters.name: padding
parameters.description: Digits of each number, padded with zeros.

parameters.name: separator
parameters.description: Text between a name and its number.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Rename the selected objects or every object in the file.

parameters.name: rename_data
parameters.description: Give single-user object data (meshes, curves, lights) the new object name.

outputs.description: Objects renamed in place; the plan is returned as a report.

limits: Renames objects and, when they have a single user, their data; materials, collections and other data blocks keep their names. Case splitting is a heuristic for ASCII words and digit runs. Names are cut to 63 bytes, so very long names lose their end. Regular expressions use Python syntax. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
technique_references: Two-pass renaming through temporary names to avoid automatic .001 suffixes
Word splitting at case changes and digit runs with regular expressions
Collision-free numbering within groups of equal names
